'''''Cytinus hypocistis''''' is an ant-pollinated<ref name="ab">{{cite journal |author1=Clara de Vega |author2=Montserrat Arista |author3=Pedro L. Ortiz |author4=Carlos M. Herrera |author-link4=Carlos M. Herrera |author5=Salvador Talavera |date=May 2009 |title=The ant-pollination system of ''Cytinus hypocistis'' (Cytinaceae), a Mediterranean root holoparasite |journal=Annals of Botany |volume=103 |issue=7 |pages=1065–1075 |doi=10.1093/aob/mcp049 |pmc=2707910 |pmid=19258337}}</ref> species of obligate<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=De Vega |first=Clara |last2=Ortiz |first2=Pedro Luis |last3=Arista |first3=Montserrat |last4=Talavera |first4=Salvador |date=2007-11-01 |title=The Endophytic System of Mediterranean Cytinus (Cytinaceae) Developing on Five Host Cistaceae Species |url=https://academic.oup.com/aob/article-abstract/100/6/1209/126707?redirectedFrom=fulltext |journal=Annals of Botany |volume=100 |issue=6 |pages=1209–1217 |doi=10.1093/aob/mcm217 |issn=0305-7364 |pmc=2759266 |pmid=17804607}}</ref> [[parasite|parasitic]] plant in the family [[Cytinaceae]] having four subspecies, which is parasitic on ''[[Cistus]]'' (rock-rose) species. It is found primarily in locations that surround the [[Mediterranean Sea]],<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | access-date=November 15, 2012}}</ref> and is the [[type (biology)|type]] for the genus ''Cytinus''.<ref name=trop>{{ cite web |url=http://www.tropicos.org/Name/40020958 |title=Name - !''Cytinus'' L. |work=Tropicos |publisher=[[Missouri Botanical Garden]] |location=[[Saint Louis, Missouri]] |quote=T: ''Cytinus hypocistis'' (L.) L.; annotation: nom. cons. |access-date=November 15, 2012}}</ref> The binomial has been [[conserved name|conserved]].<ref name=trop/>

== Description ==
''Cytinus hypocistis'' is an [[Endophyte|endophytic]] [[Parasitic plant|root holoparasite]] that has no [[chlorophyll]], external roots, leaves, or stems.<ref name=":0" /> It is a [[perennial]] that spends most of its life completely inside the root tissue of its host, and the flowers of ''Cytinus hypocistis'' are the only component of the parasite that can be seen emerging from the host root during their reproductive season.<ref name=":0" /> The sweet smelling [[inflorescence]] above ground is visited by many species of ants that [[Pollination|pollinate]] it.<ref name="ab" />

==Distribution==
''Cytinus hypocistis'' is native to [[Albania]]; [[Algeria]]; [[Crete]]; [[Croatia]]; [[Cyprus]]; [[Greece]]; [[France]] (including [[Corsica]]); [[Palestine (region)|Palestine]]; [[Italy]] (including [[Sardinia]] and [[Sicily]]); [[Lebanon]]; [[Libya]]; [[Malta]]; [[Morocco]]; [[Portugal]]; [[Spain]] (including both the [[Balearic Islands|Balearic]] and [[Canary Islands]]); [[Syria]]; [[Tunisia]]; and [[Turkey]].<ref name=grin/>

The subspecies ''C. h.'' subsp. ''macranthus'' is native to Portugal and western Spain; ''C. h.'' subsp. ''orientalis'' is native to southern Greece and Crete; and ''C. h.'' subsp. ''pityusensis'' is [[endemism|endemic]] to [[Ibiza]] of the Balearic Islands.<ref name=rbge/>

== Habitat ==
''Cytinus hypocistis'' lives within the roots of its host and relies on the rock-roses it infests as a source of water and nutrients.<ref name=":0" /> As a result of feeding on the nutrients of the host plant, ''Cytinus hypocistis'' has a negative impact on [[Productivity (ecology)|productivity]], seed viability, and overall reproductive ability in the white rockroses (''[[Cistus albidus]]'') that it parasitizes.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sánchez-Ordóñez |first=Nerea |last2=Julián |first2=Clara |last3=Jené |first3=Laia |last4=Pintó-Marijuan |first4=Marta |last5=Munné-Bosch |first5=Sergi |date=2025-06-01 |title=Influence of ''Cytinus hypocistis'' parasitism on fruit and seed production in the mediterranean shrub Cistus albidus |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0140196325000229 |journal=Journal of Arid Environments |volume=228 |article-number=105338 |doi=10.1016/j.jaridenv.2025.105338 |issn=0140-1963|doi-access=free }}</ref> 

Tenebrionid beetles (''Pimelia costata'') [[Dispersal vector|disperse]] the seeds of ''Cytinus hypocistis'' by [[Ingestion|ingesting]] them and then [[Excretion|excreting]] them in favourable underground [[germination]] sites.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=de Vega |first=Clara |last2=Arista |first2=Montserrat |last3=Ortiz |first3=Pedro L. |last4=Herrera |first4=Carlos M. |last5=Talavera |first5=Salvador |date=2011-04-01 |title=Endozoochory by beetles: a novel seed dispersal mechanism |url=https://academic.oup.com/aob/article-abstract/107/4/629/162481?redirectedFrom=fulltext |journal=Annals of Botany |volume=107 |issue=4 |pages=629–637 |doi=10.1093/aob/mcr013 |issn=0305-7364 |pmc=3064545 |pmid=21303784}}</ref> 

==Uses==
''Cytinus hypocistis'' has been used in traditional medicine to treat [[dysentery]] and [[tumor]]s of the [[throat]], and has been used for its [[astringent]] qualities.<ref name=jad>{{cite web |author=[[James A. Duke]] |title=''Cytinus hypocistis'' (RAFFLESIACEAE) |publisher=Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases |url=http://www.ars-grin.gov/cgi-bin/duke/ethnobot.pl?ethnobot.taxon=Cytinus%20hypocistis |access-date=November 15, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923174003/http://www.ars-grin.gov/cgi-bin/duke/ethnobot.pl?ethnobot.taxon=Cytinus%20hypocistis |archive-date=September 23, 2015 }}</ref>
